idiom_name: typed component interfaces in a Map/registry; generic accessors instead of casts
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds static shape checking to the object bag: components declare an interface, the entity holds a Map or array of them, and a generic accessor (get<T extends Component>(ctor: new (...a: any[]) => T): T | undefined) hands back a typed handle so call sites need no casts - the container structure is otherwise ordinary composition, and a component needs no base class because typing is structural. When the capability set is closed, a discriminated union or a registry type can make 'missing component' a compile error, but for open sets lookups still return undefined and must be handled. Dense entity populations use a data-oriented ECS (bitECS), which stores components in typed arrays indexed by numeric entity ids.
pitfalls: A Map<Function, Component> erases the concrete type, so the accessor needs one honest as T cast; keep lookups behind that generic helper instead of casting at every call site.

Compiler settings change class-field initialisation order (useDefineForClassFields with ES2022 targets runs fields before constructor bodies), so a component that reads another component while being constructed can see undefined - attach components after construction.
Keying by c.constructor silently replaces an existing component of the same type while keying by instance lets duplicates update twice; pick the policy deliberately and document it in add().
